item.test_conditions: SEM/EDS analysis of cross-section and surface morphology after oxidation
item.structure_change: Ta and W concentrated in dendrites; V and Cr enriched in interdendritic regions; Laves phase (Cr2Ta) forms network in interdendritic areas
item.property_change: Oxidation resistance improves with Cr; corrosion resistance improves with Cr; hardness increases with Cr
item.attributed_mechanism: Cr and Ta have strong binding ability (enthalpy of mixing −7 KJ/mol) forming Cr2Ta; Cr diffusion rate faster than Ta, enabling Cr2O3 formation
quotes: Ta and W with high melting points are first solidified and formed, and mainly distributed in the white dendrite area; there is a high content of V and Cr elements in the gray area.

The minimum enthalpy of mixing (−7 KJ/mol) of Cr and Ta means that during the solidification process, Cr and Ta are more easily combined to form intermetallic compounds, which leads to the formation of Cr 2 Ta in the Laves phase.
The dense oxide film inhibits the diffusion of oxygen atoms, reduces the oxidation rate, and improves oxidation resistance.
